work.title: The First Part of King Henry the Fourth
work.author: William Shakespeare

lines.text: O no, my nephew must not know, Sir Richard,
lines.plainText: O no my nephew must not know Sir Richard

lines.text: The liberal and kind offer of the King.
lines.plainText: The liberal and kind offer of the King

lines.text: 'Twere best he did.
lines.plainText: 'Twere best he did

lines.text: Then are we all undone.
lines.plainText: Then are we all undone

lines.text: It is not possible, it cannot be,
lines.plainText: It is not possible it cannot be

lines.text: The King should keep his word in loving us;
lines.plainText: The King should keep his word in loving us

lines.text: He will suspect us still, and find a time
lines.plainText: He will suspect us still and find a time

lines.text: To punish this offence in other faults.
lines.plainText: To punish this offence in other faults

lines.text: Suspicion all our lives shall be stuck full of eyes,
lines.plainText: Suspicion all our lives shall be stuck full of eyes

lines.text: For treason is but trusted like the fox,
lines.plainText: For treason is but trusted like the fox

lines.text: Who, ne'er so tame, so cherish'd and lock'd up,
lines.plainText: Who ne'er so tame so cherish'd and lock'd up

lines.text: Will have a wild trick of his ancestors.
lines.plainText: Will have a wild trick of his ancestors

lines.text: Look how we can, or sad or merrily,
lines.plainText: Look how we can or sad or merrily

lines.text: Interpretation will misquote our looks,
lines.plainText: Interpretation will misquote our looks

lines.text: And we shall feed like oxen at a stall,
lines.plainText: And we shall feed like oxen at a stall

lines.text: The better cherish'd still the nearer death.
lines.plainText: The better cherish'd still the nearer death

lines.text: My nephew's trespass may be well forgot,
lines.plainText: My nephew's trespass may be well forgot

lines.text: It hath the excuse of youth and heat of blood,
lines.plainText: It hath the excuse of youth and heat of blood

lines.text: And an adopted name of privilege—
lines.plainText: And an adopted name of privilege

lines.text: A hare-brain'd Hotspur, govern'd by a spleen.
lines.plainText: A harebrain'd Hotspur govern'd by a spleen

lines.text: All his offences live upon my head
lines.plainText: All his offences live upon my head

lines.text: And on his father's. We did train him on,
lines.plainText: And on his father's We did train him on

lines.text: And, his corruption being ta'en from us,
lines.plainText: And his corruption being ta'en from us

lines.text: We as the spring of all shall pay for all.
lines.plainText: We as the spring of all shall pay for all

lines.text: Therefore, good cousin, let not Harry know
lines.plainText: Therefore good cousin let not Harry know

lines.text: In any case the offer of the King.
lines.plainText: In any case the offer of the King

lines.text: Deliver what you will, I'll say 'tis so.
lines.plainText: Deliver what you will I'll say 'tis so

lines.text: Here comes your cousin.
lines.plainText: Here comes your cousin

content.text: Enter Hotspur and Douglas; Officers and Soldiers behind.

lines.text: My uncle is return'd.
lines.plainText: My uncle is return'd

lines.text: Deliver up my Lord of Westmoreland.
lines.plainText: Deliver up my Lord of Westmoreland

lines.text: Uncle, what news?
lines.plainText: Uncle what news

lines.text: The King will bid you battle presently.
lines.plainText: The King will bid you battle presently

lines.text: Defy him by the Lord Of Westmoreland.
lines.plainText: Defy him by the Lord Of Westmoreland

lines.text: Lord Douglas, go you and tell him so.
lines.plainText: Lord Douglas go you and tell him so

lines.text: Marry, I shall, and very willingly.
lines.plainText: Marry I shall and very willingly

lines.text: There is no seeming mercy in the King.
lines.plainText: There is no seeming mercy in the King

lines.text: Did you beg any? God forbid!
lines.plainText: Did you beg any God forbid

lines.text: I told him gently of our grievances,
lines.plainText: I told him gently of our grievances

lines.text: Of his oath-breaking; which he mended thus,
lines.plainText: Of his oathbreaking which he mended thus

lines.text: By now forswearing that he is forsworn.
lines.plainText: By now forswearing that he is forsworn

lines.text: He calls us rebels, traitors, and will scourge
lines.plainText: He calls us rebels traitors and will scourge

lines.text: With haughty arms this hateful name in us.
lines.plainText: With haughty arms this hateful name in us

lines.text: Arm, gentlemen; to arms! For I have thrown
lines.plainText: Arm gentlemen to arms For I have thrown

lines.text: A brave defiance in King Henry's teeth,
lines.plainText: A brave defiance in King Henry's teeth

lines.text: And Westmoreland, that was engaged, did bear it,
lines.plainText: And Westmoreland that was engaged did bear it

lines.text: Which cannot choose but bring him quickly on.
lines.plainText: Which cannot choose but bring him quickly on

lines.text: The Prince of Wales stepp'd forth before the King,
lines.plainText: The Prince of Wales stepp'd forth before the King

lines.text: And, nephew, challenged you to single fight.
lines.plainText: And nephew challenged you to single fight

lines.text: O, would the quarrel lay upon our heads,
lines.plainText: O would the quarrel lay upon our heads

lines.text: And that no man might draw short breath today
lines.plainText: And that no man might draw short breath today

lines.text: But I and Harry Monmouth! Tell me, tell me,
lines.plainText: But I and Harry Monmouth Tell me tell me

lines.text: How show'd his tasking? Seem'd it in contempt?
lines.plainText: How show'd his tasking Seem'd it in contempt

lines.text: No, by my soul. I never in my life
lines.plainText: No by my soul I never in my life

lines.text: Did hear a challenge urged more modestly,
lines.plainText: Did hear a challenge urged more modestly

lines.text: Unless a brother should a brother dare
lines.plainText: Unless a brother should a brother dare

lines.text: To gentle exercise and proof of arms.
lines.plainText: To gentle exercise and proof of arms

lines.text: He gave you all the duties of a man,
lines.plainText: He gave you all the duties of a man

lines.text: Trimm'd up your praises with a princely tongue,
lines.plainText: Trimm'd up your praises with a princely tongue

lines.text: Spoke your deservings like a chronicle,
lines.plainText: Spoke your deservings like a chronicle

lines.text: Making you ever better than his praise
lines.plainText: Making you ever better than his praise

lines.text: By still dispraising praise valued with you,
lines.plainText: By still dispraising praise valued with you

lines.text: And, which became him like a prince indeed,
lines.plainText: And which became him like a prince indeed

lines.text: He made a blushing cital of himself,
lines.plainText: He made a blushing cital of himself

lines.text: And chid his truant youth with such a grace
lines.plainText: And chid his truant youth with such a grace

lines.text: As if he master'd there a double spirit
lines.plainText: As if he master'd there a double spirit

lines.text: Of teaching and of learning instantly.
lines.plainText: Of teaching and of learning instantly

lines.text: There did he pause: but let me tell the world,
lines.plainText: There did he pause but let me tell the world

lines.text: If he outlive the envy of this day,
lines.plainText: If he outlive the envy of this day

lines.text: England did never owe so sweet a hope
lines.plainText: England did never owe so sweet a hope

lines.text: So much misconstrued in his wantonness.
lines.plainText: So much misconstrued in his wantonness

lines.text: Cousin, I think thou art enamoured
lines.plainText: Cousin I think thou art enamoured

lines.text: Upon his follies. Never did I hear
lines.plainText: Upon his follies Never did I hear

lines.text: Of any prince so wild a liberty.
lines.plainText: Of any prince so wild a liberty

lines.text: But be he as he will, yet once ere night
lines.plainText: But be he as he will yet once ere night

lines.text: I will embrace him with a soldier's arm,
lines.plainText: I will embrace him with a soldier's arm

lines.text: That he shall shrink under my courtesy.
lines.plainText: That he shall shrink under my courtesy

lines.text: Arm, arm with speed! And, fellows, soldiers, friends,
lines.plainText: Arm arm with speed And fellows soldiers friends

lines.text: Better consider what you have to do
lines.plainText: Better consider what you have to do

lines.text: Than I that have not well the gift of tongue
lines.plainText: Than I that have not well the gift of tongue

lines.text: Can lift your blood up with persuasion.
lines.plainText: Can lift your blood up with persuasion

lines.text: My lord, here are letters for you.
lines.plainText: My lord here are letters for you

lines.text: I cannot read them now.—
lines.plainText: I cannot read them now

lines.text: O gentlemen, the time of life is short!
lines.plainText: O gentlemen the time of life is short

lines.text: To spend that shortness basely were too long
lines.plainText: To spend that shortness basely were too long

lines.text: If life did ride upon a dial's point,
lines.plainText: If life did ride upon a dial's point

lines.text: Still ending at the arrival of an hour.
lines.plainText: Still ending at the arrival of an hour

lines.text: And if we live, we live to tread on kings;
lines.plainText: And if we live we live to tread on kings

lines.text: If die, brave death, when princes die with us!
lines.plainText: If die brave death when princes die with us

lines.text: Now, for our consciences, the arms are fair
lines.plainText: Now for our consciences the arms are fair

lines.text: When the intent of bearing them is just.
lines.plainText: When the intent of bearing them is just

lines.text: My lord, prepare. The King comes on apace.
lines.plainText: My lord prepare The King comes on apace

lines.text: I thank him that he cuts me from my tale,
lines.plainText: I thank him that he cuts me from my tale

lines.text: For I profess not talking. Only this:
lines.plainText: For I profess not talking Only this

lines.text: Let each man do his best. And here draw I
lines.plainText: Let each man do his best And here draw I

lines.text: A sword whose temper I intend to stain
lines.plainText: A sword whose temper I intend to stain

lines.text: With the best blood that I can meet withal
lines.plainText: With the best blood that I can meet withal

lines.text: In the adventure of this perilous day.
lines.plainText: In the adventure of this perilous day

lines.text: Now, Esperance! Percy! And set on.
lines.plainText: Now Esperance Percy And set on

lines.text: Sound all the lofty instruments of war,
lines.plainText: Sound all the lofty instruments of war

lines.text: And by that music let us all embrace,
lines.plainText: And by that music let us all embrace

lines.text: For, Heaven to Earth, some of us never shall
lines.plainText: For Heaven to Earth some of us never shall

lines.text: A second time do such a courtesy.
lines.plainText: A second time do such a courtesy

content.text: [The trumpets sound. They embrace, and exeunt.]
